01

“Ya Sin”

Two explanations transmitted from Mujāhid ibn Jabr and al-Ḍaḥḥāk (Q 36:1).

790
Explanation from Mujāhid No. 790: 1: 3

Mujāhid ibn Jabr

English
Transmission wording
790: 1:3. Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, on His words
"Ya Sin": He said, the openings of the speech of God, Mighty and Majestic (verse 1).
العربية
790: 1: 3 سفيان عن بن أَبِي نَجِيحٍ عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ فِي قوله (يس) قَالَ فَوَاتِحُ كَلَامِ اللَّهِ عز وجل (الآية 1) .

02

“Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life and record what they…”

Three explanations transmitted from Mujāhid ibn Jabr (Q 36:12).

792
Explanation from Mujāhid No. 792: 4: 2

Mujāhid ibn Jabr

English
Transmission wording
792: 4:2. Sufyan, from a man, from Mujahid, on His words
"Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life and record what they have put forth and their traces": He said, the traces of misguidance they left behind (verse 12).
العربية
792: 4: 2 سُفْيَانُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ فِي قَوْلِهِ إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي الموتى ونكتب ما قدموا وءاثارهم قَالَ مَا أَثَرُوا مِنَ الضَّلَالَةِ (الآية 12) .
Edition record 371487 · p. 248Link to report ↗
793
Explanation from Mujāhid No. 793: 5: 1

Mujāhid ibn Jabr

English
Transmission wording
793: 5:1. Muhammad related to us; Abu Hudhayfa related to us; Sufyan related to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, on His words
"and everything We have enumerated in a clear register": He said, in the Mother of the Book (verse 12).
العربية
793: 5: 1 حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدٌ ثَنَا أَبُو حُذَيْفَةَ ثَنَا سُفْيَانُ عَنْ لَيْثٍ عَنْ مجاهد في قوله وكل شئ أحصيناه في إمام مبين قال في أم الكتاب (الآية 12) .
Edition record 371487 · p. 248Link to report ↗

Report 794

English
794: 6:10. He said: the people of Antioch (verse 13).

06

“It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night…”

An explanation transmitted from Abū Ṣāliḥ (Q 36:40).

799
Explanation from Abū Ṣāliḥ No. 799: 10: 9

Abū Ṣāliḥ

English
Transmission wording
799: 10:9. Sufyan, from Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, on His words
"It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day, and each is floating in an orbit": He said, it is not proper for the sun to overtake the moon, meaning that night and day do not ⦗p. 250⦘ come together; "nor does the night outstrip the day": he said, it is not proper for the night to overtake the light of the day (verse 40).
العربية
الإسناد
799: 10: 9 سفيان عن اسمعيل بن أبي خلد عن أبي صلح في قوله الشَّمْسُ يَنْبَغِي لَهَا أَنْ تُدْرِكَ الْقَمَرَ وَلا اللَّيْلُ سَابِقُ النَّهَارِ وكل في فلك يسبحون قال لَا يَنْبَغِي لِلشَّمْسِ أَنْ تُدْرِكَ الْقَمَرَ يَعْنِي أَنَّ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ لا
"report__pb">⦗p. 250⦘ يجتمعان قال الليل سابق النهار قَالَ لَا يَنْبَغِي لِلَّيْلِ أَنْ يدرك ضوء النهار (الآية 40) .
Edition record 371488 371489 · pp. 249–250Link to report ↗
